# `runtime` operations

11 operations. Generated from `assets/operations.json`; [all areas](README.md).

### runtime.start

**Connect native runtime**

Start or reuse the single native display session for this device. Repeated calls return its existing session ID. Supports Android, physical iPhone from Linux, and Apple Simulator on an optional SSH Mac. With TOMACCO_FIXTURE_RUNTIME set, device fixture:NAME connects the offline scripted fixture of that name (transport fixture, evidence fixture), for tests and the benchmark runner only.

Annotations: writes, idempotent, open world.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | string | yes |  | one of `android`, `ios` |
| `device` | string | yes |  | non-empty, up to 200 characters |
| `remote` | string |  |  | Optional configured Mac workspace for an Apple Simulator; omit for a physical iPhone on Linux. |
| `server` | string |  |  | Optional scrcpy 4.1 server JAR override. |
| `fps` | integer |  | `60` | 1 to 60 |
| `bit_rate` | integer |  | `12000000` | 100000 to 50000000 |
| `runner_bundle_id` | string |  | `""` | Installed WebDriverAgent runner identifier for a physical iPhone. |
| `runner_mode` | string |  | `"xctest"` | one of `xctest`, `external`; xctest: start the signed WDA runner through go-ios; external: WDA is already running on the selected USB device. |
| `audio` | boolean |  | `true` | Forward Android output audio to this computer using a session-owned scrcpy playback job. Does not capture a microphone. Unsupported audio leaves video connected and reports audio failure. |

```sh
tomaccoctl call runtime.start '{"platform":"android","device":"<device>"}'
```

### runtime.audio

**Stream device audio**

Start, stop or inspect Android output audio playback on this computer without restarting the app or display session. Repeated starts reuse one playback job. Stops restore the device audio route; they do not mute the device itself. Requires Android 11+ and scrcpy.

Annotations: writes, idempotent, open world.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | string | yes |  | Connected Android runtime session ID. |
| `action` | string |  | `"status"` | one of `start`, `stop`, `status` |

```sh
tomaccoctl call runtime.audio '{"session":"<session>"}'
```

### runtime.state

**Runtime status**

Read actual runtime dimensions, video counters, transport errors and input_capabilities: whether touch streams live or is sent as an atomic trace, how many contacts, pinch, fill, rotate, capture and hierarchy.

### runtime.input

**Native input**

Deliver native input using normalized 0..1 coordinates. Android supports touch/tap/swipe/key/text/rotate; text pastes UTF-8. Physical iPhone uses WDA for Unicode text/fill, tap/swipe/rotate, a two-finger pinch (x, y, scale, duration) and gestures committed as one atomic request on touch-up; shake/hinge are unsupported there. Android also takes pinch, as two scrcpy pointers. Apple Simulator supports ASCII HID text and Unicode accessible fill; extra gestures depend on the companion. Pass decoded width/height after Simulator rotation. An AirPlay session (device airplay) drives the iPhone as a Bluetooth pointer and US-layout keyboard once it is paired with Tomacco and AssistiveTouch is on: touch moves the pointer relatively, hover moves it without a button, cancel without a button forgets the last position; tap, swipe, text and the keys home, volume_up, volume_down, enter, escape, backspace, delete, tab and the arrows work. fill with verify_value checks the focused editor and reads its exact value back before answering verified (USB iPhone over WebDriverAgent and scripted fixtures; others answer fill_verification_unsupported). runtime.state answers input_capabilities per transport; runtime.gesture sends timestamped traces.

Annotations: writes, not idempotent, open world.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | string | yes |  | matching `^[a-f0-9]{32}$`; ID returned by runtime.start; separate from desktop preview sessions. |
| `action` | string | yes |  | one of `touch`, `tap`, `swipe`, `key`, `text`, `fill`, `rotate`, `shake`, `pinch`, `hinge` |
| `phase` | string |  |  | one of `down`, `move`, `up`, `cancel`, `hover` |
| `x` | number |  |  | 0 to 1 |
| `y` | number |  |  | 0 to 1 |
| `x2` | number |  |  | 0 to 1 |
| `y2` | number |  |  | 0 to 1 |
| `duration` | number |  | `0.3` | 0.01 to 5 |
| `key` | string |  |  | one of `home`, `back`, `escape`, `enter`, `backspace`, `delete`, `tab`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `power`, `volume_up`, `volume_down`, `apps` |
| `text` | string |  |  | up to 16000 characters |
| `orientation` | string |  |  | one of `portrait`, `portrait_upside_down`, `landscape_left`, `landscape_right` |
| `scale` | number |  |  | 0.05 to 20 |
| `angle` | number |  |  | 0 to 180 |
| `width` | integer |  |  | 1 to 16384 |
| `height` | integer |  |  | 1 to 16384 |
| `verify_value` | boolean |  |  | For fill: verify it (off when left out). The editor that takes the focus after the tap must cover the tapped point (or be named by field_name) and be a supported text field; its value is read before writing (an already matching value is not typed again; a value equal to the placeholder never counts as entered text) and read back afterwards on the same session and element. Answers verified, or an error: nothing typed (field_not_focused, field_wrong_target, field_unsupported, field_stale, field_unobservable, field_tap_failed), or field_uncertain when text was sent and its effect is unknown; nothing is ever retyped. Secure fields are refused unread. Transports that cannot read an editor back answer fill_verification_unsupported and send nothing (input_capabilities.fill_verification) |
| `field_name` | string |  |  | non-empty, up to 256 characters; For a verified fill: the editor must have this accessibility identifier or label (for a field that moves as it takes the focus); otherwise it must cover the tapped point |
| `focus_timeout_ms` | integer |  |  | 0 to 10000; For a verified fill: how long to wait for the editor to take the focus after the tap (2000 when left out) |
| `submit` | boolean |  |  | For a verified fill: send one Return to the field once its value is verified (or already matched) and it still has the focus; never on any other outcome. Check where it led with an expect postcondition or a fresh observation |

```sh
tomaccoctl call runtime.input '{"session":"<session>","action":"touch"}'
```

### runtime.observe

**Observe a session**

One fresh look at a connected session, for an agent about to act: a full-resolution PNG frame with its id (the first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256), captured_at, capture_ms and age_ms (0 at capture; add the time since captured_at before acting), the geometry the frame was taken in (width, height, orientation, rotation, and for an iPhone the point size and scale) with the coordinate spaces inputs and screen.\* use, the foreground app with home_screen, the keyboard, the input focus, the transport's input_capabilities and a one-line context. Every part names its source. What the transport cannot observe is {available:false, reason}, never a guess: Android reads dumpsys window and dumpsys input_method, a USB iPhone asks WebDriverAgent for the active app, a keyboard element and the active element, the Simulator and AirPlay report no app or keyboard, and AirPlay captures no frame. Over MCP the PNG is embedded. A fixture session answers evidence fixture.

Annotations: writes, not idempotent, open world.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | string | yes |  | matching `^[a-f0-9]{32}$`; ID returned by runtime.start; separate from desktop preview sessions. |
| `path` | string |  |  | non-empty; Absolute PNG path for the frame; by default observe.png in the session's directory, replaced each time |
| `context` | boolean |  | `true` | Also read the foreground app, keyboard and focus (one or two transport calls); false answers the frame and geometry only |

```sh
tomaccoctl call runtime.observe '{"session":"<session>"}'
```

### runtime.gesture

**Timestamped gesture trace**

Deliver one or more contacts as timestamped traces in 0..1 of the frame: each contact's points with t_ms from its touch-down. The answer's mode says what the transport did: atomic_trace (a USB iPhone submits the whole trace as one WebDriverAgent actions request, deterministic but not live) or live (Android, the Simulator and the fixture replay the events with host timing, one contact after another by time). Multi-contact traces need a transport whose input_capabilities (runtime.state) allow it; AirPlay answers an error. Use runtime.input touch for an interactive drag that follows a pointer.

Annotations: writes, not idempotent, open world.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | string | yes |  | matching `^[a-f0-9]{32}$`; ID returned by runtime.start; separate from desktop preview sessions. |
| `contacts` | array of object | yes |  | 1 to 5 items; The fingers, each a trace of 2 to 240 points |
| `contacts[].points` | array of object | yes |  | 2 to 240 items |
| `contacts[].points[].x` | number | yes |  | 0 to 1 |
| `contacts[].points[].y` | number | yes |  | 0 to 1 |
| `contacts[].points[].t_ms` | integer | yes |  | 0 to 10000; Milliseconds since this contact touched down; non-decreasing |

```sh
tomaccoctl call runtime.gesture '{"session":"<session>","contacts":[{"points":[{"x":0,"y":0,"t_ms":0},{"x":0,"y":0,"t_ms":0}]}]}'
```

### runtime.actions

**Ordered input batch**

Run up to 50 input and wait steps in order on one session, in one call, with a result per step. A text step waits until a field has the focus (polling the session's focus and keyboard) before it types, so the first characters are not lost, and answers focus_timeout with nothing typed when no field takes it; where the transport cannot report focus it says so and settles briefly instead. A tap can name a mark from the last screen.marks of this session and is verified like screen.tap. A step may carry expect, a text that must appear or go afterwards: met makes the step verified, otherwise postcondition_failed stops the batch with the step still counted as applied. A fill step with verify_value is verified only when the field's exact value was read back; text sent with an unknown effect makes it uncertain (field_uncertain) and it is never sent again. The first failure stops the rest: the error's details list every step so far (steps), the indexes that reached the device (applied_steps), those whose effect is unknown (uncertain_steps) and those not run (skipped), so an agent never resends an applied step. The whole batch is bounded by timeout and by the client's cancellation. With frame (width, height, orientation from runtime.observe) the batch is refused with frame_stale and nothing sent when the screen's geometry changed since. observe_after appends a fresh runtime.observe. The answer's evidence is fixture on the offline fixture runtime.

Annotations: writes, not idempotent, open world.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | string | yes |  | matching `^[a-f0-9]{32}$`; ID returned by runtime.start; separate from desktop preview sessions. |
| `steps` | array of object | yes |  | 1 to 50 items |
| `steps[].action` | string | yes |  | one of `tap`, `swipe`, `key`, `text`, `fill`, `pinch`, `rotate`, `gesture`, `wait`, `wait_text`, `wait_text_gone`, `wait_stable`, `observe`; tap (x, y or mark), swipe, key, text (after the field has the focus), fill (verify_value reads the value back), pinch, rotate and gesture change the device; wait, wait_text, wait_text_gone, wait_stable and observe only look |
